model_annotation: Figure 4 presents a bar chart illustrating the frequency with which enterprises perceive certain measures as essential for limiting the “shadow economy” in the country. The horizontal axis categorizes the measures into distinct textual labels, listed in an alphabetical order, without any specific visual indication of a numerical sequence or ranking. The vertical axis represents frequency, quantified in percentages, with a linear scale ranging from 0% to 100%, marked at regular intervals of 20 percentage points (0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%). The bars are arranged in ascending order of their height from left to right, indicating the frequency of selection for each measure. The tallest bar corresponds to a value of approximately 80%, while the shortest bar reaches approximately 20%. The bars are visually distinct from each other through their height and color, with no additional visual emphasis such as shading or outlining applied to any specific bar. The chart lacks a legend or explicit labeling of the bars to identify which measure corresponds to each bar, and the text accompanying the figure describes the measures listed but does not provide a direct visual correspondence to the chart’s bars.
